July, 2024
Author: Vishal Mishra

 At Jabalpur

 Shri Manish Datt - Senior Advocate with Shri Prateek Tiw
 Advocate for appellant.

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Shri Sourabh Shukla - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/St
Heard on admission.
The appeal is admitted for hearing.
Heard on I.A. No.16294 of 2023 - an application for suspension of sentence.

2. This is the first application seeking for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellant - Suresh @ Mintu Vishwakarma who has been convicted under Sections 376 (2)(L), 450 and 506 Part II o f the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to R.I. for 10 years, 7 years and 1 year respectively and fine of Rs.5,000/-, Rs.1,000/- and Rs.1,000/- respectively, with default stipulations as mentioned in the impugned judgment dated 28.06.2023 passed by the II Additional Sessions Judge, Beena District Sagar in S.T.No.13/2019.
3.

entities.text: II Additional Sessions Judge, Beena District Sagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is innocent and has not committed any offence in any manner.
The victim is a major.
It is argued that the victim is a consenting party.
The report was lodged after 6 months of the incident.
There is no explanation for delay.
It is pointed out that when she developed pregnancy she narrated the incident to her family members.
Thereafter, the FIR was got registered.
He was on bail during trial and has not misused the liberty granted by the Court.
There is no likelihood of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
The appellant is ready to abide by all the terms and 2 CRA-8727-2023 conditions that may be imposed by this Court while considering his application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
4. P e r contra, learned Panel Lawyer for the State has opposed the contentions pointing out the fact that there is specific participation of the appellant in the commission of the offence.

It is submitted that the threatening was given by the appellant to kill the family members if the matter is reported to any one on that basis there was delay in trial but the fact remains that there is no explanation for Suresh @ Mintu Vishwkarma vs State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87117220/
1 delay for a period of more than six months.
5.

entities.text: Suresh @ Mintu Vishwkarma vs State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court deems it appropriate to allow the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

6. Accordingly, I.A. No.16294 of 2023 is allowed and it is directed that the remaining jail sentence of the appellant shall remain under suspension subject to the verification for the fact that the amount of fine has been deposited and he b e released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the trial Court/concerned Court on 16.12.2024 and thereafter on such other subsequent dates as may be fixed in that behalf.
List for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.

(VISHAL MISHRA) JUDGE AM 3 CRA-8727-2023 Suresh @ Mintu Vishwkarma vs State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87117220/
